emerging_technology: Agentic AI built on large language models (LLM-based agents that plan, use tools, and complete multi-step tasks)
intended_application: Proposed bounded applicant-support workflow: retrieve approved program information, ask clarifying questions, plan next steps, and request a counselor appointment through a permission-limited tool. Staff approve outbound messages and any record changes. Excludes admission, scholarship, visa and eligibility decisions.
organization: Hypothetical small private college - Office of Admissions (synthetic low-readiness profile; not an observed institution)
industry_sector: Higher education - graduate and professional admissions and recruitment. Applicant trust, privacy, accessibility and accuracy matter; international applicants include EU residents; exact legal obligations require specialist review.
business_need: Reduce repetitive inquiry handling and improve timely guidance through the staged path the Adoption specialist permits for this application class: a proof of concept now, then a gated bounded experiment (C4). Actual demand, response time and benefits have not been measured.
users_stakeholders: Prospective students; admissions director and two counselors (the whole office); college president (sponsor); outsourced IT managed-service provider; part-time compliance counsel
adoption_posture: Moderate / fast-follower (held constant across the primary and both contrasts; for NYU SPS this is a course-case assumption, not an official policy).
capabilities_constraints: Synthetic profile: the college president proposed the agent after a conference and asked admissions to 'make it happen this cycle'; no budget line exists beyond vendor licences, and a hiring freeze is in place. Three staff (the admissions director and two counselors) handle email, phone, events and application processing; the director reports email backlogs of several days in peak weeks. Web-inquiry volume is about 150 per week. IT is outsourced to a managed-service provider that handles tickets but not integrations; the CRM is a vendor-hosted basic tier without API access. The college has no written policy on using AI with applicant data and no AI review process; compliance counsel is part-time. There is no chatbot today. One counselor position was eliminated last year, and staff have said they worry automation will be used to justify further cuts.
risk_consequence_context: Wrong deadlines or promises can harm applicants, and the organization is accountable for what its agent says (D21); unauthorized actions can expose data. No applicant records are used in this assignment. No legal determination is made.
